framework.name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023
framework.description: The first international standard specifying requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) within the context of an organisation. Based on the ISO High Level Structure (Annex SL) for compatibility with other ISO management system standards. Includes normative requirements and an informative Annex A of extended controls.

requirements.title: Section 4 — Context of the Organisation
requirements.text: The organisation shall determine external and internal issues relevant to its AI purposes and objectives. It shall identify interested parties and their requirements relevant to the AIMS. The organisation shall understand the AI context including the AI policy framework and societal context in which AI systems are developed and used.

controls.description: Document internal and external context relevant to the organisation's AI activities
Identify and document interested parties and their AI-related requirements and expectations
Define the scope of the AIMS, including boundaries and applicability

requirements.title: Section 5 — Leadership
requirements.text: Top management shall demonstrate leadership and commitment by taking accountability for the effectiveness of the AIMS; ensuring AI policy and objectives are established; promoting a culture of responsible AI; and ensuring integration of AIMS requirements into the organisation's business processes. An AI policy shall be established, communicated, and maintained.

controls.description: Evidence of top management commitment to the AIMS, including AI policy endorsement
Publish, implement, and communicate an AI policy aligned to the organisation's AI objectives
Assign and communicate AIMS roles, responsibilities, and authorities

requirements.title: Clause 6.1.2 — AI Risk Assessment
requirements.text: The organisation shall establish, implement, and maintain an AI risk assessment process that: identifies AI-related risks and opportunities; analyses risk likelihood and impact; evaluates risks against risk criteria; considers AI system impacts on people and society; and documents results. The risk assessment shall include AI system impact assessment as per Annex A controls.

controls.description: Establish and operate a documented AI risk assessment process
evidence_needed: Risk assessment records per AI system

controls.description: Assess impacts of AI systems on individuals, groups, and society
Maintain a risk register covering all in-scope AI systems

requirements.title: Clause 6.1.3 — AI Risk Treatment
requirements.text: The organisation shall select and implement appropriate risk treatment options for AI risks, produce an AI risk treatment plan, and obtain approval for the plan and acceptance of residual risks from risk owners. Treatment options include: applying controls; avoiding the AI activity; sharing risk; or accepting risk.

controls.description: Develop and implement an AI risk treatment plan for all identified AI risks
Obtain documented risk acceptance from designated risk owners for residual risks

requirements.title: Clause 8.4 — AI System Impact Assessment
requirements.text: The organisation shall carry out AI system impact assessments to identify and evaluate potential impacts of AI systems on individuals and groups. Impact assessments shall consider: impacts on rights and freedoms; environmental impacts; societal impacts; and impacts specific to vulnerable groups. Results shall be documented and inform system design decisions.

controls.description: Conduct documented impact assessments for each AI system covering rights, freedoms, and societal impacts
Consider impacts on vulnerable groups including children, elderly, and protected characteristics
Use impact assessment results to inform design, development, and deployment decisions
evidence_needed: Design decision records linked to impact assessments

requirements.title: Clause 8.5 — AI System Lifecycle
requirements.text: The organisation shall plan, implement, and control the processes needed for the AI system lifecycle including: design and development; procurement and acquisition; deployment and integration; operation and monitoring; and decommissioning. The organisation shall document lifecycle stages and apply appropriate controls at each stage.

controls.description: Define and document AI system lifecycle stages and applicable governance controls for each stage
Apply security, privacy, and bias controls throughout the AI development and deployment lifecycle
Define and execute a decommissioning plan when AI systems are retired

requirements.title: Clause 9.1 — Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis, and Evaluation
requirements.text: The organisation shall determine what needs to be monitored and measured, including AI system performance; methods for monitoring, measurement, analysis, and evaluation; when the monitoring and measuring shall be performed; and when the results shall be analysed and evaluated. Documented information shall be retained as evidence of the results.

controls.description: Define KPIs and monitoring metrics for each AI system in production
Conduct periodic performance evaluations and document results
Implement automated alerting for performance degradation or anomalous behaviour

requirements.title: Annex A.2 — Policies for AI
requirements.text: The organisation shall establish policies relating to AI as part of the AIMS to define principles, requirements, and responsibilities for responsible AI development and use. Policies shall address: AI ethics principles; acceptable use of AI; data governance for AI; human oversight requirements; and AI transparency.

controls.description: Establish and communicate an AI ethics policy covering fairness, transparency, accountability, and privacy
Define acceptable use of AI systems with explicit prohibited use cases
Establish a data governance policy specific to AI training and operation

requirements.title: Annex A.3 — Internal Organisation
requirements.text: The organisation shall define its internal organisation for AI governance including: a designated AI governance function or role; cross-functional AI review processes; escalation paths for AI-related issues; and clear accountability for AI decisions.

controls.description: Establish a designated AI governance function (committee, board, or role) with documented terms of reference
Define clear accountability for AI decisions at the individual system level

requirements.title: Annex A.4 — Resources for AI
requirements.text: The organisation shall ensure adequate resources for responsible AI including: competent AI practitioners; data science and ethics expertise; legal and compliance capability for AI regulation; compute infrastructure with appropriate security controls; and ongoing training budget.

controls.description: Assess and maintain AI competence requirements across technical, ethical, legal, and governance dimensions
Provide ongoing AI training and awareness for all staff involved in AI activities

requirements.title: Annex A.5 — AI System Impacts on Individuals and Society
requirements.text: The organisation shall identify and address potential negative impacts of AI systems including: discrimination and fairness harms; privacy violations; safety impacts; environmental impacts from compute; manipulation and deception risks; and impacts on human agency and decision-making autonomy.

controls.description: Conduct fairness assessments covering protected characteristics for each AI system
Assess and mitigate privacy risks in AI system design and operation
Assess environmental impact of AI compute and implement mitigation measures

requirements.title: Annex A.6 — AI System Lifecycle Management
requirements.text: The organisation shall implement controls across the full AI system lifecycle including: requirements specification; design and development; testing and validation; deployment and monitoring; change management; and decommissioning. Responsible AI principles shall be embedded at each lifecycle stage.

controls.description: Maintain a documented requirements specification for each AI system including ethical requirements
Implement a change management process for AI system updates that includes re-assessment of risks
Conduct model validation and testing before production deployment

requirements.title: Annex A.7 — Data for AI Systems
requirements.text: The organisation shall implement data controls for AI covering: data quality assurance; data lineage and provenance tracking; bias assessment in training data; personal data protection in AI datasets; dataset versioning and documentation; and controls for third-party data used in AI.

controls.description: Implement data quality controls and document quality criteria for AI training and inference data
Maintain data lineage and provenance records for AI training datasets
Implement controls for personal data used in AI consistent with applicable privacy regulations

requirements.title: Annex A.8 — Information for Interested Parties
requirements.text: The organisation shall provide appropriate information to interested parties about AI systems including: disclosure of AI use; model capabilities and limitations; decision rationale (explainability); rights to contest AI decisions; and contact information for AI governance enquiries.

controls.description: Implement user disclosure mechanisms for AI-generated content and AI-driven decisions
Provide explainability for consequential AI decisions to affected individuals
Establish and communicate a process for individuals to contest AI-driven decisions

requirements.title: Annex A.9 — Log and Audit
requirements.text: The organisation shall implement logging and audit capabilities for AI systems to support: operational monitoring; incident investigation; regulatory compliance; and internal audit. Logs shall capture sufficient information to reconstruct AI system decisions and shall be protected against unauthorised modification.

controls.description: Define and implement logging requirements for each AI system covering inputs, outputs, and decision context
Protect AI system logs against tampering and ensure appropriate retention
Conduct regular internal audits of AI systems against AIMS requirements

requirements.title: Annex A.10 — Stakeholder Engagement
requirements.text: The organisation shall engage with relevant stakeholders including: users of AI systems; affected communities; regulators; suppliers and third-party AI providers; and internal staff. Engagement shall inform AI design, deployment, and governance decisions.

controls.description: Establish a stakeholder engagement programme for AI governance
Manage third-party AI suppliers with appropriate governance controls including contractual obligations
